name: Venus Legacy
lead: Venus Legacy is a Venus Concept radiofrequency device for non-surgical skin tightening, wrinkle reduction and body contouring; Wikipedia lists it among commercial RF skin-tightening devices [1]. Grokipedia describes it as a multipolar RF system that adds pulsed electromagnetic fields and pulsed suction, used for laxity, wrinkles, cellulite and mild fat reduction on the face and body [2].

A 2015 article in the Journal of Clinical and Aesthetic Dermatology presented Venus Freeze and Venus Legacy as newer RF devices within the trend toward noninvasive skin tightening [3]. Published evidence available for this article is limited to that review and small registered studies.
infobox: Multipolar RF with pulsed electromagnetic fields and suction (in-office)

paras: According to Grokipedia, Venus Legacy combines multipolar radiofrequency with pulsed electromagnetic field energy and pulsed suction [2]. Wikipedia lists Venus Legacy and Venus Freeze Plus as Venus Concept's RF devices [1].

Category-wide reports on RF devices include pain, dents from uneven healing, and rare fat necrosis or atrophic scarring [1]. Grokipedia lists redness, swelling, burns and hyperpigmentation as reported effects and pacemakers and pregnancy as contraindications [2].

A 2015 review article presented Venus Freeze and Venus Legacy within the category of noninvasive RF skin tightening [3]. Registered studies on ClinicalTrials.gov include a 10-participant study combining CoolSculpting with Venus Legacy technology for flank fat and laxity (started 2015) [4] and a 50-participant study of RF and pulsed electromagnetic fields after liposuction (started 2018) [5]. Results of these registrations are not summarised here.

card.summary: Venus Concept's multipolar RF plus pulsed-magnetic-field device for skin tightening and contouring, with thin published evidence.
card.note: Evidence is limited to a short review and small registered studies.

quick.overview:
Venus Legacy is a clinic-based device from Venus Concept that combines radiofrequency, pulsed electromagnetic fields and suction. It is used for skin laxity, wrinkles and body contouring.

The published evidence found is a 2015 overview article and a couple of small registered studies.
quick.mechanism: Radiofrequency heats tissue to prompt collagen remodelling, with pulsed fields and suction added by the manufacturer's design.
quick.risks: Reported RF effects include redness, swelling, pain, burns and pigment change, and rarely scarring or fat loss. Pacemakers and pregnancy are listed contraindications.
